name: Juan Perón
role: Argentine general and three-time president, founder of Peronism (1895–1974)
summary: Perón led Argentina from 1946 to 1955 and again from 1973 to 1974. He built Justicialism as a Third Position between capitalism and communism, with social rights, state direction of the economy, a social function for property, a Catholic constitution, and a strong presidency with unlimited re-election, and his government pressed the opposition press.

public-ownership.rationale: Article 40 declared natural resources inalienable and provided for transferring public services to the state.

unions-good.rationale: Article 37 wrote the right to join unions freely into the constitution.

property-fundamental.rationale: Article 38 subjects property to a social function.

state-harmful.rationale: The 1949 constitution gives the state a leading role in the economy through intervention and monopolies.

decide-locally.rationale: The 1949 reform made provinces adjust their constitutions to the national government.

traditional-family.rationale: Article 37 protects the family and treats the family as a protected institution.

more-religion-public.rationale: His constitution required a Catholic president while his government later ended religious instruction in state schools.

gradual-change.rationale: The Modelo argentino describes a peaceful revolution of gradual change led by ideas.

limit-growth.rationale: The 1972 message says the so-called progress must have limits and condemns waste of resources.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The 1972 message calls technology a double-edged weapon and a mirage.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Article 40 authorised state intervention in the economy, and created state monopolies.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Article 38 gives farmers the chance to own the land they work.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: The Modelo argentino describes a peaceful revolution in which ideas replace violence.

separate-church-state.rationale: His constitution kept state support of the Catholic cult while his government later ended religious instruction in state schools.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The Modelo argentino condemns egoism and sets a solidary community model against it.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Twenty Truths put the homeland first but also call for a fair balance between individual and community rights.

limit-population.rationale: The 1972 message calls for planned population growth by safe methods, but exempts Argentina.

organic-representation.rationale: The Modelo argentino keeps political parties and adds functional groups beside them rather than replacing them.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Third Position was announced in defence of the sovereignty and self-determination of small nations.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Twenty Truths call for national unity and the end of civil strife and name workers as the one class.

dominated-front.rationale: He called for a Third World and Latin American unity against the blocs.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Article 28 of the 1949 constitution establishes equality before the law without racial differences.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: His government introduced religious teaching in state schools and then repealed it in 1955.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The 1949 constitution added a state of prevention and alert that restricted rights without going through Congress.

party-controls-media.rationale: His government seized La Prensa in 1951 and built a quasi-state media empire.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Article 78 set a six-year term with immediate re-election allowed.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The Third Position rejected alignment with either bloc.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Twenty Truths call for an economically free and politically independent Argentina.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Article 82 replaced the electoral college with direct election of the president.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Article 38 gives property a social function and Article 39 places capital at the service of the national economy.

elective-rulers.rationale: Article 82 has the president elected by the people.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The Modelo argentino treats foreign capital as only a complement to national development.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The 1972 message says profit and waste can no longer be the basic motor of any society.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: He defended non-intervention, including over Guatemala in 1954.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He presented the Third Position as a path between capitalism and communism.

suppress-opposition.rationale: His government pressured its opponents, as the account of its final years records.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He announced the Third Position in defence of small nations against the blocs.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: He said he would cut off his hand before signing a loan with the IMF.

term-limits.rationale: The 1949 reform removed the bar on consecutive terms, so the president faced no term limit.

women-suffrage.rationale: Ley 13010 gave women the same political rights as men.

national-church-status.rationale: Article 2 has the federal government support the Catholic cult and Article 77 requires a Catholic president.

equal-conscription.rationale: Article 5 of Ley 13010 exempts women from military obligations.

national-resource-control.rationale: Article 40 made mineral and energy resources inalienable national property and reserved their exploitation to the state.

multipolar-world.rationale: The Modelo argentino calls for a pluripolar world.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: The Twenty Truths say work is a right and a duty because each should produce at least what he consumes.

small-step-social-reform.rationale: The Modelo argentino describes a peaceful revolution of gradual change led by ideas.

notes: Most statements are null because the sources read give no stated position or record on them.
